extracted.intended_audience: authors, illustrators, publishers, librarians, and awards committee members involved with children's informational books (Sibert Award)
extracted.subtask_description: Terms and criteria governing eligibility and selection of the Robert F. Sibert Informational Book Award for the most distinguished informational book for children published in the U.S. in English during the preceding year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award scope and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sibert Award is presented annually to the author, author/illustrator, co-authors, or author and illustrator named on the title page of the most distinguished informational book for children published in the United States in English during the preceding year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies who (as named on the title page) receives the award and the geographic/language/publication-year scope of eligible books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible genres: poetry and traditional literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry and traditional literature (e.g., folktales) are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no other limitations as to the character of the book providing it is an original work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor books may be named
rubrics_metrics.description: Honor books may be named. They are books that are also truly distinguished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee may designate one or more honor books in addition to the award winner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author eligibility: U.S. citizen or resident
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is restricted to authors, author/illustrator, co-authors, or author and illustrator named on the title page who are citizens or residents of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Resident' definition for what constitutes a resident (established and maintained residence, not a casual visitor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Original work requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "Original work" means that the text (or illustrations, as applicable) was created by this writer or artist and no one else. Further, it means the text (or illustrations) is presented here for the first time and has not been previously published elsewhere in this or any other form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text or illustrations reprinted or compiled from other sources are not eligible. Abridgements are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-published-in-U.S. requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "First published in the United States" means that books first published in previous years in other countries are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books published simultaneously in the U.S. and another country may be eligible. Books published in a U.S. territory or U.S. commonwealth are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement: In English
rubrics_metrics.description: "In English" means that the committee considers only books written and published in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement DOES NOT limit the use of words or phrases in another language where appropriate in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication-year eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: "Published in the preceding year" means that the book has a publication date in that year, was available for purchase in that year, and has a copyright date no later than that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A book might have a copyright date prior to the year under consideration but was not published until the year under consideration. If published prior to its year of copyright as stated in the book, it shall be considered in its year of copyright as stated in the book. The intent is that every book be eligible once and only once.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee consideration limited to eligible books
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee is to consider in its deliberations only books eligible for the award as specified in the terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phrase 'only the books eligible for the award' specifies that the committee is to consider only eligible books, not an author’s body of work or previous accolades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award may be given posthumously
rubrics_metrics.description: The award may be given posthumously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Informational books
rubrics_metrics.description: "Informational books" are defined as those written and illustrated to present, organize, and interpret documentable, factual material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Significant contribution (what it gauges)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Significant contribution" is gauged by how well the work elucidates, clarifies and enlivens its subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee considers overall accuracy, documentation, organization, visual material and book design when judging significant contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Children's literature (intended audience)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Children’s literature" is defined as the body of books published for an intended and potential child audience. Such books display respect for children’s understanding, abilities, and appreciation. Children range from birth through age fourteen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books for the entire range are to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Distinguished
rubrics_metrics.description: "Distinguished" is defined as noted for significant achievement; marked by quality, excellence, or eminence; distinctive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Author and Illustrator crediting
rubrics_metrics.description: "Author" and "Illustrator" may include co-authors or author-illustrators. Illustrator may include persons credited on the title page for visual material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility follows the names as printed on the title page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Resident
rubrics_metrics.description: "Resident" is defined as someone who has established and maintains a residence in the United States, U.S. territory, or U.S. commonwealth as distinct from being a casual or occasional visitor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellent, engaging, and distinctive use of language
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members consider excellent, engaging, and distinctive use of language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the set of elements and qualities used to identify the most distinguished informational book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellent, engaging, and distinctive visual presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members consider excellent, engaging, and distinctive visual presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual material and book design are explicitly part of evaluation under 'significant contribution.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate organization and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members consider appropriate organization and documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports clarity and trustworthiness of factual material (indexes, bibliographies, source notes as relevant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, accurate, and stimulating presentation of facts, concepts, and ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members consider clear, accurate, and stimulating presentation of facts, concepts, and ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy and stimulation (engagement) both matter for informational content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate style of presentation for subject and intended audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members consider an appropriate style of presentation for subject and for intended audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone, complexity, and presentation should match the subject matter and children's comprehension levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive features
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members consider supportive features (index, table of contents, maps, timelines, etc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These features aid usability and understanding of informational content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respectful and of interest to children
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members consider whether the book is respectful and of interest to children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books should display respect for children's understanding, abilities, and appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not every element must be excellent; relevance matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Not every book relies equally on every element. The committee need not find excellence in every element listed above but only in those relevant to the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation is contextual: emphasis is on elements appropriate to the book's aims and format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-contained work requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The book must be a self-contained entity, not dependent on other media for enjoyment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books that require external media (e.g., websites, apps) to be enjoyed may not meet this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award purpose: not for didactic intent or popularity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sibert Award is presented to honor distinguished informational books for children. The award is not presented for didactic intent or for popularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational intention or popularity alone do not justify the award; distinction in the listed qualities is required.
